evidence: The hunk shows commit() calling writeConfigText then writeHistory with no handling between them, so a history failure reports a failed click over a landed edit. The reviewer's own fallback option was 'wrapping this failure mode with a message that says the edit succeeded but isn't undoable', and record() in 0241cca does exactly that while correctly keeping file-first order. Flag false positive: bca461d only changed CRLF handling in json5-edit.ts; commit() is original PR code.
guidance_note: The agent had already logged this exact write-then-record gap as an issue comment at 09:03; when you note a known failure mode before review, fix its message in the original PR instead of filing it for the record.

evidence: The hunk shows writeFileSync(tmp) then renameSync(tmp, file) with only a log-and-rethrow catch, so a failed rename orphans the tmp. 0241cca adds writeAtomic with rmSync(tmp, {force:true}) on failure and uses it for both the config file and the history file. Flag false positive: bca461d did not touch writeConfigText; the tmp+rename code is original.
guidance_note: When writing tmp+rename twice in one module, factor it into one helper with failure-path cleanup the first time rather than spelling it per caller.

evidence: The reviewer is right that a first-match entryOf edits a value JSON5 ignores, and the agent correctly saw that findLast is also wrong for reset because deleting the last duplicate promotes the first. It took the reviewer's 'reject duplicate keys' option, though document-wide rather than 'for a path', which is what F11 later questions. Flag false positive: bca461d's json5-edit changes are EOL-only; the Scanner and entryOf are original.
guidance_note: When writing a span-preserving editor over a format whose parser tolerates duplicates, decide duplicate-key semantics in the original scanner and write down the blast radius of the choice.

evidence: The original undoEdit pops state.past's last entry regardless of file, while sessionConfigFile resolves different files per session, so undo from project A could revert project B. 0241cca keys HistoryState by file and adds a two-file test; removing the per-entry file field so an entry cannot name a file other than its stack is a real types-are-the-program move. Flag false positive: bca461d did not touch history code.
guidance_note: When a write target is resolved per session, key every derived store (history, caches) by that same target in the original design instead of keeping one daemon-global stack.

evidence: A preset declaring no root renders the config's own root, edit mode's +/- write that same path, and deleting it falls back to the bundled default root through mergeWithDefault, so reset does not 'delete the whole bar'; the round-1 summary independently confirmed the ↺ gate uses the same declares-root rule. Refusing reset would leave a '-' edit with no undo but a hand edit. The pushback did not examine the 'declared nowhere' fallthrough in the same expression, which F8 found next round. Flag false positive: placementOf is original code untouched by bca461d.
guidance_note: When defending a fallback branch against a review, enumerate every input that reaches that branch (here: preset declared in file, bundled, or nowhere) before calling it by design.

evidence: 0241cca rewrote config-file-store.ts, verbs/index.ts, CLAUDE.md and docs to per-file history but left action.ts's 'ONE GLOBAL history... single stack' comment. The agent swept four more sites in f0a8c8c, though it still missed the docs table row F10 found.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a concept's cardinality (global to per-file), grep the whole tree for the old wording ('global history', 'single stack') in the same commit, not only the files the fix touched.

evidence: The user-facing loader error still says undo 'steps the ONE global history over every durable config edit', which became false once 0241cca keyed history by file. It is the same drift as F6, raised in the same round.
guidance_note: When a fix changes semantics, sweep user-facing error strings as well as comments and docs for the old description.

evidence: The original declaresRoot is `has(doc, own) ? ... : RAW_PRESETS[preset]?.root !== undefined`, so a custom preset deleted from the file reads as 'declares no root' and the write or delete lands on the file's top-level root. fab3c19 adds a typed Declaration that throws on 'declared nowhere', with a verb-level test. Flag false positive: 4eb7e0d changed only CLAUDE.md and docs, and this expression is byte-for-byte original PR code, though it sits in the same branch F5's pushback defended.
guidance_note: When a lookup falls back from 'declared in file' to 'declared in bundle', write the third case (declared in neither) as an explicit refusal in the original code instead of letting `?.` fold it into the false arm.

evidence: writeValue/deleteValue/applyLayoutOp read with readFileSync and write synchronously with no await in between, so a requireFileState re-check would close nothing: it is the same unlocked read-compare-write. Undo/redo check because their snapshot is from an earlier click, which is the distinction the agent drew. Flag false positive: record() came from F1's refactor, but the unconditional write predates review and 4eb7e0d is docs-only.

The vocabulary-table row still says undo steps 'the config file's global edit history', which contradicts the doc's per-file section that 0241cca rewrote. F6's sweep named docs/interaction-authoring.md:667 but missed line 86, so the drift from F4 survived two fix commits.
guidance_note: When sweeping stale wording, search for each distinct word of the old concept ('global', 'single', 'one history') across the file rather than fixing the lines the reviewer and one grep happened to surface.

evidence: 0241cca's check in Scanner.object() throws on any duplicate in any object, and docOf parses the whole file on every durable click, so a duplicate in an untouched segment now blocks every persist, reset, undo and layout op on a file that JSON5.parse renders fine. The agent declined the path-scoped check for a defensible reason (it would leave entryOf's first-vs-last ambiguity in place for the day the edit passes through) and filed the real gap, the late surfacing, as a load-time advisory ticket. The reviewer's 'regression' framing is overstated, since durable writes to this file are new in this PR.
guidance_note: When choosing a whole-document refusal at a parse boundary, ask in the same fix how the user learns about the defect before it blocks them, and ship the load-time diagnostic with it.

evidence: fab3c19 moved the 'cannot persist ...' error from ensureAuthored, which only persist-style writes reach, into declarationOf inside placementOf, which deleteValue (reset) and applyLayoutOp also call. The fix's own new test fires a reset through it, and its regex only matched the suffix, so the wrong verb went unnoticed.
guidance_note: When a fix moves an error into a function shared by more callers, reread the message for each new caller, and make the test assert the full message rather than a suffix.

evidence: The comment saying a hand-edited-file refusal is 'surfaced the same way' as the BadVerbArgs empty-stack case was already present before 0241cca (it is unchanged context there), and requireFileState throws a plain Error. The agent made the comment true by moving BadVerbArgs below the store and throwing it for stale-click refusals, which is the reviewer's first option. Flag false positive: fab3c19 did not touch verbs/index.ts; the comment is original.
guidance_note: When a comment claims two failure paths are classified the same way, check that both throw the same error class before committing the comment.

evidence: This PR's own CLAUDE.md redefines `.preset.customized` as 'the config FILE authors a root at the active preset's root path', and check.ts already has the file through loadConfig's `raw`, so hardcoding false makes check's returned render diverge from the daemon's for a file that authors that root. The agent's 'fixture like term.cols' analogy fails because term.cols cannot be derived from the file and this value can. The impact is limited to example output, since the second pass exercises the true branch. Flag false positive: fab3c19 did not touch check.ts; the comment rewrite is original PR code.
guidance_note: When a PR redefines a derived flag as a pure function of the file, update every caller that hardcoded it to call the derivation, rather than rewriting the old justification comment.

evidence: checkPresetRootTarget rejects a preset-root persist that lacks a tree op, but nothing rejects a tree op on a globals or segment-palette persist, so `{ persist: 'padding', removeSegment: 'foo' }` loads and fails only at click time. The agent added the mirror check with tests. Flag false positive: fab3c19 did not touch cross-ref.ts; the one-directional check is original (only renamed from rootOps in this PR).
guidance_note: When writing a pairing validator between two enums, write the accept/reject table for both directions (A requires B, and not-A forbids B) before writing either check.

evidence: The reviewer reports collectSegmentNames is imported and never referenced in the test file, and the agent removed it. Flag false positive: fab3c19 did not touch dsl-edit-mode.test.ts.

The hunk shows setConfig calling writeValue before releaseSessionKey, which can throw BadVerbArgs on a reloaded state registry, so the click reports failure over a durable write that landed. This is F1's 'failure reported after the edit landed' class one layer up, which F1's fix to record() did not sweep. The code is original PR code, not introduced by fab3c19. The agent moved validation before the write and the release after it.
guidance_note: When fixing 'click fails after the durable write landed' in one function, audit every verb handler for fallible steps sequenced after the durable write and validate them before it.

narrative: This is a large rewrite that made the config file the durable store. Round 0 raised five real issues in original code; four fixes were sound and one pushback (F5) was correct. The F4 per-file history fix left 'global history' wording in a comment, an error string and a docs table row, which cost all of round 1 (F6, F7) and part of round 3 (F10, after F6's sweep missed a row). F3's whole-document duplicate-key refusal produced F11, F8's fix moved an error message under new callers (F12), and F17 is F1's landed-but-reported-failed class in the verb handlers. Most of round 3 (F13-F16) was original code the first rounds did not reach, so only round 1 is purely fix-caused.
guidance_observations: When a fix changes a concept's cardinality or name, one tree-wide grep for every word of the old phrasing would have removed round 1 and F10.
The F5 pushback defended a fallback branch without enumerating every input that reaches it, and the next round found the 'declared nowhere' input in the same expression (F8).
The agent's pre-review issue comment already named the F1 gap and closed it as 'filed for the record'; known failure modes noted before review should be fixed or ticketed, not narrated.

evidence: The hunk shows `state: this.buildState(cwd, null)` built unconditionally in getOrCreate, which a successful first load then disposes and the no-file path rebuilds identically. c0a6f5c makes loadFromDisk return a typed LoadOutcome and builds the default only when that outcome failed; replacing a correlated (state, error) mutation pair with a union is an apt types-are-the-program use. Rounds 1 and 2 found nothing new in render.ts.
guidance_note: When making a field non-null by seeding it with a fallback, build the fallback only on the path that needs it (outcome ?? fallback), not eagerly at construction.

evidence: The claim depends on composeWithDiagnostics in server.ts appending a warning row after the error block's file:// row, and the packet does not include server.ts. The agent agreed and narrowed the doc to 'the error block closes with the file:// link', a strictly weaker claim that is safe whether or not the ordering is as described.

narrative: This small PR made CacheEntry.state non-null by seeding it with the bundled default. Round 0 raised two advisories, an eager double-build of the default and an overstated doc claim about the strip's last row. Both were fixed in one commit, and rounds 1 and 2 found nothing new, so no fix introduced a finding.
guidance_observations: One fix commit addressed both findings and the following rounds were clean, so this PR's review process shows no wasted cycle.
